stem: Make $x$ the subject of the formula $y = {=a}px + {=b}qx$.
solution: $x$ is in both terms on the right-hand side, so take it out as a common factor: $y = x({=a}p + {=b}q)$.
$x$ is now multiplied by the bracket. Divide both sides by $({=a}p + {=b}q)$: $\frac{y}{{=a}p + {=b}q} = x$.
notes: Entry point of the skill, modelled on book question ex4-5-9 (E = mgh + 1/2 mv^2, solve for m): the subject appears in exactly two terms, nothing else is on the subject's side, so the whole job is factorise then divide. Letters p, q, x, y are fixed; only the two coefficients a and b (2 to 9, different) change, giving 56 distinct stems. Coefficients are at least 2 so no '1px' is ever printed. Every instance's answer is x = y/(ap + bq); the denominator is never 0 because p and q are letters (the book's own note on restrictions, ex4-5-9, is not asked of the student here). No mcq, so no distractors and the catalogued misconception is not used.
